# Pilot Detection Checklist

Status: Validated
Specification Version: v2
Frozen: true
Type: General
Current Pass: 2

## Commandment Scores

| Pass | Commandment | State | Score | Why | Why not 100% | Escalated | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Problem First | Stable | 90% | Reporting team already runs a manual Friday review; pilot formalizes an existing cadence rather than inventing new process. | Slight ambiguity on whether "review" covers only alert triage or broader reporting. | No | Scoped to alert/detection inspection only. |
| 1 | Constraints | Stable | 90% | Owner explicitly declined automation for the pilot and accepted the resulting delay (D1). | Long-term intent (post-pilot) not specified, but out of scope here. | No | D1 recorded as approved decision. |
| 1 | Stakeholders | Stable | 90% | Owner self-assigned as the accountable party for inspecting missed alerts. | No backup/escalation contact named. | No | Accepted as pilot-scale; single-owner model. |
| 1 | Harmony | Stable | 85% | Manual cadence, accepted delay, and self-assigned ownership are mutually consistent — no automation implied anywhere. | First-pass check; downstream sections not yet drafted. | No | Reconfirmed consistent in Pass 2. |
| 2 | Success Criteria | Stable | 95% | User explicitly defined "done" as presence of four named items plus absence of automation. | Verification method for "presence" not yet distinguished from checklist authorship itself. | No | Captured in Validation Contract. |
| 2 | Verification | Stable | 90% | Deliverable is a static checklist; verification is a direct read-through against the four required items. | No independent reviewer specified beyond the owner. | No | Owner doubles as verifier for this pilot. |
| 2 | Execution Readiness | Stable | 95% | All four required content items, scope boundary (no automation, no systems change), and ownership are explicit and unchanged since D1. | None material. | No | — |
| 2 | Harmony | Stable | 95% | Requirements, constraints, and success criteria all reaffirm the same D1 tradeoff with no contradiction introduced this pass. | Minor: blind spot (delay risk) accepted rather than mitigated. | No | Recorded under Known Blind Spots. |

## Problem Statement

The reporting team needs a lightweight, non-automated pilot checklist documenting how detection review will run manually via the existing Friday process, including the owner-accepted detection-delay tradeoff and the follow-up inspection cadence. No system or tooling changes are introduced.

## Requirements

### R1
Checklist must document the Friday manual review as the sole detection mechanism for the pilot.

### R2
Checklist must document the explicitly accepted maximum 7-day detection delay (per D1).

### R3
Checklist must document the owner (self-assigned) as accountable for inspecting missed alerts.

### R4
Checklist must document the review cadence: inspection of missed alerts occurs after two Fridays.

## Constraints

### C1
No automation is introduced during the pilot (per D1 — automation explicitly declined).

### C2
The checklist is the only deliverable; no systems, tooling, or process infrastructure changes occur.

## Success Criteria

### S1
The checklist document contains all four items (R1–R4) and contains no automation language, tooling references, or systems-change content.

## Validation Contract

### Acceptance Tests
Read the completed checklist and confirm each of R1–R4 is present as a distinct, identifiable item.

### Regression Checks
Confirm no automation-related content has been introduced in any revision of the checklist (since none exists today, any addition of automation language is a regression).

### Failure Signals
- Any of the four required items (R1–R4) is missing or unclear.
- Automation, tooling, or systems-change language appears anywhere in the checklist.

### Verification Methods
Manual read-through of the checklist by the owner (or a specify-stage reviewer) confirming presence of all four items and absence of automation content.

### Feedback Loop Design
The deliverable is a static document, so the "in-progress" signal is immediate: the checklist can be read and checked against R1–R4 as soon as drafted, at effectively zero cost. The operational fallback signal (for the process the checklist describes, not the checklist itself) is the owner's own inspection of missed alerts after two Fridays, per R4.

### Known Blind Spots
Up to 7 days of detection delay is an accepted risk (D1); real-world alerts within that window may go unnoticed until the Friday review or the two-Friday inspection catches them. This is explicitly accepted, not mitigated.

## Inputs

Existing manual Friday review process (unchanged); owner's explicit tradeoff decision (D1).

## Outputs

A single checklist document containing R1–R4.

## Out of Scope

Any automation, tooling, or systems changes; anything beyond the pilot checklist itself.

## Authority Boundaries

### Executor May Decide
Formatting/layout of the checklist document.

### Executor Must Escalate
Any request to introduce automation or systems changes during the pilot.

### Executor Must Not Change
The 7-day accepted delay, the manual-only constraint (D1), or the two-Friday inspection cadence.

## Current Interpretation

Produce a single checklist artifact for the pilot that documents an existing manual process (Friday review), a previously accepted delay tradeoff (up to 7 days, D1), explicit ownership (self-assigned), and a fixed follow-up inspection point (after two Fridays) — with no automation or systems change introduced.

## Misclassification Risks

### Potential False Positives
A checklist that looks complete but omits the explicit numeric delay (7 days) or buries ownership/cadence in vague language would appear done while failing S1.

### Potential False Negatives
None outstanding — user has reconfirmed all four required items and declared no change since D1; no critical omissions identified this pass.

## Ambiguities

### Blocking
None remaining.

### Non-Blocking
Exact document format/template for the checklist (left to executor discretion).

### Intentional
Long-term (post-pilot) automation decision is intentionally out of scope; D1 applies to the pilot only.

## Risks

Missed alerts during the up-to-7-day delay window; accepted explicitly by the owner as the pilot's tradeoff (D1).

## Stakeholders

Owner (self-assigned, accountable for inspecting missed alerts and executing the two-Friday review).
